content.title: Where to watch the Masters Round 3: Tee times, TV, live streams
content.text: Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy looks to repeat as the Masters champion with a six-stroke lead heading into Round 3 today. Find out how to watch for free. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Robert Fenbers, cleveland.comAUGUSTA, Ga. - The 2026 Masters continues with the third round today – Saturday, April 11 – at Augusta National Golf Club in Augusta, Georgia. Today’s round is available on multiple streaming services. What time does the Masters start today? The 2026 Masters continues with the third round on Saturday, April 11, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern. What is the Masters TV schedule today?Third Round - Saturday, April 11All times Eastern.Start time: 9:30 a.m.TV: 2-7 p.m. on CBSStreaming: 8 a.m.-6 p.m. on ESPN Streaming and 12-2 p.m. on Paramount Plus and 2-7 p.m. on FuboTV How to watch the Masters for freeFuboTV, which offers a free trial, starts at $73.99. You may cancel before the free trial ends to avoid being charged. If not, you can get $25 off your first month. Fubo includes access to more than 185 sports, entertainment and news channels. You can record games, TV shows, movies and more.Paramount+ lets you watch multiple sports like golf, soccer, UFC and NFL at a significantly lower price than most streaming services. They offer the essential package for $8.99 a month and the premium package for $13.99 a month. In addition to CBS, it also features programming from BET, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon, MTV and more. Take in the ultimate Masters streaming experience with PGA TOUR LIVE on the ESPN app. Catch every swing with the Unlimited Plan for $29.99 per month (or $299.99 for entire year) and the Select Plan for $12.99 per month (or $129.99 for entire year).What is PGA Tour Live? PGA TOUR LIVE expanded through ESPN coverage features over 3,200 new hours of live streaming and multiple live feeds available. The live coverage features over 35 tournaments, including the Masters. What happened in Round 2 of the Masters?Defending champion Rory McIlroy dominated the field with -7 under par in Round 2, opening up a historic six-stroke lead heading into the third round. He made birdies on six of his last seven holes, sealing the largest 36-hole lead in Masters history. McIlroy’s -12 under leads Sam Burns and Patrick Reed, who are both tied for second. Shane Lowry, Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose are a distant fourth with -5 under par.
